1.why: Body text is a clean sans-serif and codes are monospaced with ample line height and padding, though letter spacing is standard rather than notably generous.

2.why: All instructions appear as short sentence-case strings with no italics, no all-caps prose, and no dense paragraphs (the monospace log is supplementary test output, not instruction).

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card layout with large text that maps cleanly to phone width, although only desktop-width screenshots were provided to confirm.

4.why: Every screen uses at most one short plain-language sentence, e.g. 'Create a test-only secret, then add it manually to your authenticator app.'

5.why: Only the mobile-number field shows a format placeholder (+44 7700 900000); the recovery-code field gives no example of the expected XXXXX-XXXXX format.

6.why: No step requires reading more than a sentence or a short bulleted code list to proceed; the longer monospace log is optional test-only output.

7.why: No copy button or download is offered for the 32-character setup secret or the recovery-code list, and the setup screen explicitly instructs manual entry into the authenticator app.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative is offered at any step; step 03 states the secret must be added manually.

9.why: Login uses standard email/password inputs that browsers can normally autofill, but nothing visible demonstrates autocomplete attributes or password-manager/one-time-code support.

10.why: The bold page heading and single blue primary button make the action clear, but the breadcrumb trail (Sign in → Identity → Authenticator → Recovery codes) never highlights which step is current.

11.why: Each enrolment screen requests a single action; only the post-enrolment settings hub shows three buttons, visually differentiated by colour (blue, grey, red).

12.why: Status banners plainly state outcomes and next steps ('MFA is enabled. Save these one-time codes now.', 'Recovery code accepted.'), though the settings hub itself gives no what-comes-next guidance.

13.why: The user can retry after the generic error and regenerate recovery codes without any lockout, and codes are always displayed in full, but there is no reveal/hide toggle (e.g. for the masked password).

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming and suggests a retry but never explains what the actual problem was.

15.why: No countdown, session-expiry warning, or reading time limit appears on any screen, though the time-based authenticator code (logged as 228551) inherently rotates within a short window.
